moments.title: Comiskey Park opens
moments.text: The White Sox moved into their new ballpark at 35th St and Shields Ave, their home for the next 80 years.

moments.title: 98 cents and a disco record
moments.text: For a White Sox and Tigers doubleheader, fans who brought a disco record got in for 98 cents. Tens of thousands filled the park, and an estimated 20,000 more were left outside.

moments.title: The records blow up, the fans pour in
moments.text: Between games, WLUP disc jockey Steve Dahl blew up a crate of records in center field. An estimated 7,000 fans stormed the field; at least nine people were hurt and 39 were arrested.

moments.title: The Sox forfeit
moments.text: American League president Lee MacPhail ruled the unplayed second game a forfeit win for Detroit.

moments.title: Old Comiskey comes down
moments.text: After the White Sox moved into a new ballpark across 35th St, the old park was torn down and its site paved for parking.

moments.title: Today: home plate in a parking lot
moments.text: A plaque in the parking lot north of Rate Field marks old Comiskey's home plate, inscribed "Comiskey Park 1910-1990."

facts.label: Crowd
facts.note: Estimates range up to almost 60,000, with about 20,000 more outside.

facts.label: Arrests
facts.note: At least nine injuries were reported.

checked.notes: Date, 98-cent admission, Dahl, and the forfeit ruled by Lee MacPhail the next day confirmed (MLB.com, HISTORY, Baseball-Reference). Crowd figures vary (50,000 to almost 60,000 inside); about 7,000 on the field per WGN; at least nine injured and 39 arrests per HISTORY. Comiskey opened July 1, 1910 and was demolished in 1991; home plate plaque in the lot north of Rate Field (HMdb, Baseball Pilgrimages). Story confirmed; no changes.
